message.content:
**Hydrogen – Key Physical & Chemical Properties**

| Property | Value / Description | Notes |
|----------|---------------------|-------|
| **Atomic number** | 1 | Only element with one proton. |
| **Atomic mass** | ~1.008 u (average) | Dominated by protium (¹H). |
| **Isotopes** | ¹H (protium, 99.98 %), ²H (deuterium, 0.02 %), ³H (tritium, trace) | Deuterium used in heavy‑water reactors; tritium is radioactive (half‑life ≈ 12.3 yr). |
| **Electron configuration** | 1s¹ | One valence electron → highly reactive. |
| **Electronegativity (Pauling)** | 2.20 | Highest among elements, but still less than many nonmetals. |
| **First ionization energy** | 13.598 eV (1312 kJ mol⁻¹) | Highest of all elements. |
| **Electron affinity** | –0.754 eV (–72.8 kJ mol⁻¹) | Negative value indicates energy release when gaining an electron. |
| **Boiling point** | –252.87 °C (20.28 K) | Extremely low; boils at 20 K under 1 atm. |
| **Melting point** | –259.16 °C (14.01 K) | Sublimes at 14 K under 1 atm. |
| **Density at STP** | 0.08988 g L⁻¹ | Lightest gas; less dense than air. |
| **Molar volume at STP** | 22.414 L mol⁻¹ | Standard molar volume for ideal gases. |
| **State at room temperature** | Gas | Colorless, odorless, tasteless. |
| **Bonding** | Forms H₂ (diatomic) via covalent bond; can form hydrides (ionic or covalent). | H₂ is the most abundant molecule in the universe. |
| **Oxidation states** | +1 (most common), –1 (in hydrides), 0 (in H₂). | In compounds, hydrogen usually behaves as +1. |
| **Reactivity** | Highly reactive with many elements; reacts with oxygen to form water (exothermic). | Combustion: 2 H₂ + O₂ → 2 H₂O (ΔH ≈ –286 kJ mol⁻¹). |
| **Flammability** | Extremely flammable; wide flammability range (4 %–75 % in air). | Flame color: pale blue. |
| **Solubility in water** | ~1.6 g L⁻¹ at 25 °C | Low solubility; dissolves more in cold water. |
| **Spectral lines** | Lyman series (UV), Balmer series (visible), Paschen series (IR) | Fundamental for astrophysical spectroscopy. |
| **Role in stars** | Fusion of H into He powers stars; proton–proton chain and CNO cycle. | Energy source of the Sun. |
| **Applications** | Fuel cell technology, rocket propellant, industrial hydrogenation, ammonia synthesis (Haber process). | Clean energy potential. |

---

### Quick Highlights

- **Lightest element**: Atomic mass ≈ 1 u; density < 0.1 g L⁻¹.
- **Highest ionization energy**: Requires 13.6 eV to remove its single electron.
- **Extremely low boiling/melting points**: Substantial quantum effects; liquefies only at cryogenic temperatures.
- **Highly reactive**: Forms H₂ gas, reacts violently with oxygen, and forms a wide variety of hydrides.
- **Astrophysical importance**: Most abundant element; spectral lines used to identify hydrogen in stars and interstellar space.
- **Energy carrier**: Hydrogen fuel cells produce electricity with only water as by‑product.

Feel free to ask if you’d like deeper details on any specific property or application!
